clue.text: Garment corporation in a predicament

parts.note: tights are a garment worn on the legs
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, so it gives POT

explanation.surface: A clothing company has got itself into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business to go with the garment, but here it is the old joke word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tight spot is an idiom for being stuck in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Three maids, not evenly in step

indicators.note: not the even letters, so the odd-numbered ones are taken from three maids

explanation.surface: Three maids walking out of time with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A tread is a footstep or the sound of walking.

clue.text: Legal imbroglio about one old astronomer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the letter for one
an imbroglio is a confused muddle, so the letters of legal are muddled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A legal tangle involving one astronomer of long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbroglio' rearranges LEGAL to GALLE; 'about' puts I inside it, giving GALILE, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo was the Italian scientist who used a telescope to study the heavens in the 1600s.

clue.text: End period in a hypertension centre

parts.note: a term is a period of time
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of hypertension is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A stint at a clinic for high blood pressure comes to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to a close or finish.

clue.text: Getting ready to start to pay compensation

indicators.note: the start of the word pay is its first letter

parts.note: reparation is compensation for a wrong

explanation.surface: Gearing up to begin paying damages.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparation is the process of making things ready.

clue.text: Sounds like a square meal

indicators.note: the clue says the letter is heard spoken out loud

parts.note: a T-square is a drafting tool, so square can stand for the letter T

explanation.surface: Something that sounds like a hearty dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a square meal' is a phrase for a filling dinner; split it so 'square' is T and 'meal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon or evening repast in Britain.

clue.text: Verdi breaks a journey

indicators.note: the composer's name is broken apart and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The composer Verdi interrupts a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a trip made by car, so it is a kind of journey.

clue.text: Briefly, do the same thing

explanation.surface: Doing likewise, in short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is the written short form of this word in lists, hence 'Briefly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation do. stands for this word, which marks a repetition of what is above.

clue.text: Russian secret policeman, interrupting in Portuguese, perhaps

indicators.note: the policeman's name breaks into the word in

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police

explanation.surface: A Soviet agent butts in among Portuguese people.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal shares the Iberian peninsula with Spain, so a Portuguese person is an example.

clue.text: Indicate liability extremely plainly

parts.note: to express is to show or indicate

indicators.note: the extremes of liability are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: State clearly what one's liability is.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressly means in a clear, explicit way.

clue.text: Amplify in General Assembly

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so the letters of the word general are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A UN body turns up the volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General Assembly' reads as the UN body; 'Assembly' is the anagram signal working on 'General'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge something is to make it bigger, which is what amplifying does.

clue.text: Start to tack in a new direction before turning to port

indicators.note: the start of the word tack is just its opening letter

parts.note: W is the compass direction west

indicators.note: turning means the word for before is read backwards

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: A sailor tacks onto a new course before heading to the left side of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses PRE to ERP. 'Port' reads as the left side of a ship, but it is the definition: a harbour city in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp in Belgium is one of Europe's biggest seaports.

clue.text: Capital of the Spanish state

parts.note: del is Spanish for 'of the'
HI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Hawaii

explanation.surface: Madrid, the capital of Spain's nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for Madrid; instead 'of the' is put into Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi (New Delhi) is the seat of India's government, its capital city.

clue.text: Rita hoped to become a goddess

indicators.note: the letters of Rita hoped change into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Rita wished to be deified.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite was the Greek deity of love and beauty.

clue.text: Article written in a rest period, as often as not

indicators.note: the article is written inside the phrase for a rest period

parts.note: half-time is the break in a football match
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A piece written during a break in play.
explanation.definitionFit: Half the time is an idiom for frequently, on about every second occasion.

clue.text: Letter from a royal house

explanation.surface: A letter sent from a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Shuffle in the back row!

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: People in the back row shifting seats.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to change the order of things, as shuffling cards does.

clue.text: Attending every race, whatever happens

parts.note: to be at something is to attend it
all events means every race at a sports meeting

explanation.surface: A keen racegoer turns up to every meeting, come what may.
explanation.definitionFit: At all events is an idiom meaning in any case, regardless of circumstances.

clue.text: Six, the time in Europe to shut up shop in other words

indicators.note: the time zone closes off the word, coming at its end

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a deli is a delicatessen shop
CET is Central European Time

explanation.surface: Six o'clock, continental time, is when shops close.
explanation.walkthrough: VI and DELI come first; 'to shut up' puts CET at the end, closing the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Videlicet, abbreviated viz, is Latin for namely, introducing a restatement.

clue.text: Felt grateful for being recognized

explanation.surface: Someone was thankful to be acknowledged.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate something is to value it with thanks, and also to understand or be aware of it fully.

clue.text: Smoking smell upset boxer outwardly

indicators.note: the boxer goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upwards

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A boxer upset by a smoky odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a dog breed, but it is short for pugilist; 'upset' works because this is a down clue, so the smell reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffing is drawing on a pipe or cigarette, smoking it.

clue.text: Used to attract attention in America, for example

definitions.text: Used to attract attention in America

explanation.surface: An American exclamation for getting noticed, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: In US speech, a call of 'say!' grabs someone's notice; it also introduces an instance, like 'e.g.'

clue.text: Staying power of Army minister in S Africa

indicators.note: the army and minister pieces go inside the letters for S Africa

parts.note: SA is South Africa
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: Endurance of a military official in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is endurance, the strength to keep going.

clue.text: Quotation for a share ex-capitalisation

indicators.note: ex means without, so the word loses its capital, its opening letter

parts.note: a preference share is a kind of company share that pays dividends first

explanation.surface: A price quoted for a share after a rights issue, in stock-market jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ex-capitalisation' sounds like finance jargon but means take off the capital (first) letter of PREFERENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference is a passage cited from a source, as a quotation is.

clue.text: Roof of missing East German providing temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the word of goes missing from the word roof

parts.note: Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: Without a roof, an East German finds somewhere to stay for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roof of missing' reads as an odd phrase but says take OF out of ROOF, leaving RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds rest for the night, a short-term lodging.

clue.text: Minimum of a pound each way

parts.note: L (from Latin libra) stands for a pound
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: The smallest bet: a pound each way on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each way' is a betting term (win or place), but here it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the smallest amount possible, the minimum.

clue.text: Children's game about making a cross

parts.note: tig is the British name for tag, the chasing game
on can mean about, concerning

explanation.surface: Children playing a game with a cross drawn on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the hybrid offspring of a tiger and a lioness.

clue.text: Objectionable to oneself -a little!

annotationWithheld.why: Objectionable to oneself -a little! (7): the only reading is NO (objection) + I (oneself) + SOME (a little), which needs 'Objectionable' as both definition and the source of NO

clue.text: Before the rehearsal, take a part

indicators.note: a part is taken from the words, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Before the dress rehearsal, actors get a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere is a poetic word meaning prior to.

clue.text: Chucking out the piano, being irritated

indicators.note: out means the letter for piano is thrown away from the word

parts.note: pitching means throwing or chucking
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Throwing the piano out of the house, in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Itching describes a skin that is irritated and wants scratching.

clue.text: Disease contracted by king

parts.note: ER stands for Edward Rex, a king
a person who contracts an illness has got it

explanation.surface: A monarch caught an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a disease clue 'contracted' looks like part of the definition, but it is wordplay meaning caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal infection of rye and other cereals.

clue.text: Oriental with tiny ears suffering a sort of muscular fatigue

parts.note: E stands for east, as in oriental

indicators.note: the letters of tiny ears suffer and are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An Asian person with small ears in pain from tired muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye-strain is tiredness of the eye muscles from overuse.
